title: A tuning vent printed open
summary: A 2.1 mm vent on the crown of the rump is part of the whistle as printed. Plug it with wax and the closed note falls 90 cents; ream it to 3.5 mm and the note rises 89 cents in the solve (78 cents by the closed form). One print can be trimmed down or up.

rejected.value: a blind pilot, drilled out after printing
rejected.why: a one-sided trim: it can only raise the note, and published instruments miss the closed form in both directions, so a first print can land sharp as well as flat

returns_if.text: when measured prints of this whistle land flat every time

rejected.why: the closed note then rests on the window alone, the part the model predicts worst (10 % typical on published instruments); the trims left are filing the labium back and pouring wax into the chamber, and neither is undone

returns_if.text: when one measured print has fixed the window's end factor and the next print lands inside the 8 % band untrimmed

rejected.value: a 1.5 mm horizontal vent in the chest skirt (the character-first concept)
rejected.why: a finger can cover it there (about 146 cents flat in the panel's review) and a 1.5 mm horizontal hole may print shut

returns_if.text: when the crown of the rump is needed for something else; the vent then goes back to a place the hand does not reach

body: What the vent does not cover: a first print can miss by about 10 %, 165 cents, and the vent reaches 89 or 90 cents each way. It brings a miss of up to about 5 % back to 340 Hz, and a miss of up to about 13 % back inside the 8 % band. A miss of 15 to 20 % means a reprint with a corrected window.
